prompt:
Read the supplied document in a fresh context. Use only information in the document; do not guess missing case facts or invent rules. Rule presentation order does not create a priority. Null is unknown, not an empty set. If multiple completions allowed by the document give different answers, use underdetermined. A reported eligibility label supplies that label but not the underlying facts, rules, or derivation. For the counterfactual, add counterfactual_add to the person's actual facts while keeping all other facts and the policy unchanged. Return just one JSON object with exactly these fields:
{"active_rules":"Array of remaining active rule identifiers, or null if not uniquely determined.","answer":"yes | no | conflict | underdetermined","counterfactual_answer":"yes | no | conflict | underdetermined","facts":"Array of actual fact identifiers, or null when not supplied.","priority":"Array of [higher rule, lower rule] pairs, or null when not supplied.","rules":"Array of objects {id, if: [predicate identifiers], then: conclusion}, or null when not supplied."}
CARRIER_READER_INPUT_JSON:
{"counterfactual_add":"p00","text":"The complete actual fact set is p00. All unlisted predicates are false.
Rule r1 concludes eligible when all of p00 hold.
Rule r3 concludes eligible when all of p01 hold.
Rule r2 concludes not_eligible when all of p02 hold.
Priority: r1 overrides r2.
A rule fires exactly when all its conditions are actual facts. Only the stated priority applies, and only when both rules fire. A lower-priority fired rule is suppressed; all other fired rules remain active. Only eligible active means yes; only not_eligible active, or none active, means no; both active means conflict."}
